cell.label: Patient presenting with knee pain and a history and physical examination suspicious for patellar dislocation. Is patella present in femoral groove?
Evaluation with MRI, ultrasound, and/or plain films to evaluate for presence of osteochondral fracture and loose bodies. Is large osteochondral fracture (>15 mm) present?
Is there a loose body present?
Nonoperative therapy with patella stabilizing orthotic and progressive range of motion and strengthening exercises. Redislocation or continued symptomatic patellar instability?
Surgical evaluation for potential arthroscopic or open procedure.
With knee fully extended apply pressure on the lateral/posterior aspect of patella until it returns to femoral groove. (Anesthesia may be required.)
